tools.name: find_businesses
tools.description: Search the DouxProcess Directory for US businesses by what the person needs (roofer, electrician, insurance agency...) and where (a city and state, a ZIP, or a state). Returns the matches in the published ranking order with license, how it was checked, phone, website and listing page. covered=false

tools.name: get_business
tools.description: One business's details: licenses with their basis (issuer_file = matched against the issuer's own published file on checked_at; stated = given by the business, not yet matched, send the person to source_url), contact, whether it takes requests, and its own agent addresses (MCP and A2A).

tools.name: verify_license
tools.description: Look up a license by number, business name or phone and say which listings carry it and how it was checked. When nothing matches, tell the person to check the issuer's own lookup; never say a license is valid without a match.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Every category with its id, NAICS 2022 code, plain name, Google Business Profile names, how many listings it has, and whether requests for it are sent (health is listed but never routed).

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask in plain words ('licensed electrician near 92101 who does EV chargers') and get a short answer built only from listings, plus the businesses it rests on, in the published order. Same rules as find_businesses: no ranking or recommendation language, coverage stated honestly.

tools.name: request_contact
tools.description: Sends the person's request to the ONE business they chose, so it can reply to them. Only claimed listings take requests, and health businesses never do. Before calling, show the person this sentence and get their agreement: 'I agree that DouxProcess sends my name, my contact details and this request

tools.name: request_service
tools.description: Open the request form for one business the person chose (ChatGPT local services Get Quote). The form shows the consent sentence and sends only when the person ticks it. For a business that does not take requests it shows the business's own phone and website.

tools.name: license_history
tools.description: A California contractor license's record in the CSLB's public file, and every change since the directory began reading it daily: status and suspensions, workers' comp type and dates, bond amounts and dates, classes, expiry. Give a CSLB license number or a listing link. It never includes an insurer,

tools.name: watch_licenses
tools.description: Emails the person a link to watch these CSLB licenses: once they open it, they get one short email on any day something changes on one (status, workers' comp, bonds, classes, expiry). Nothing is watched until the person opens the link. Use the person's own email, only when they asked. Free watches 2

tools.name: verify_business
tools.description: Is this business licensed, bonded and insured today, from the government record. Give a listing slug, a license number, or a business name with its two-letter state. Returns licensed, bonded and insured as true, false or null (the record does not say), each with its source, checked_at day and record

tools.name: watch_business
tools.description: Emails the person a link to watch up to 25 listings free: once they open it, they get one short email on any day the board's record changes (status, workers' comp, bonds, classes, expiry). CSLB contractors only. Use the person's own email, only when they asked. Before calling, show them this and get

tools.name: book_estimate
tools.description: Books an estimate visit with ONE contractor the person chose whose listing shows luma.books_online. The contractor calls the person to confirm the time. Call it once without consent to get consent_text, show it, and call again with consent=true only if they agree.

findings.detail: Description of "request_contact" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: watch_licenses, verify_business, watch_business · Private data: get_business, request_contact, license_history, verify_business, watch_business, request_quotes · Public sink: get_business, watch_licenses, watch_business.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: watch_licenses, verify_business, watch_business · Private data: get_business, request_contact, license_history, verify_business, watch_business, request_quotes · Public sink: get_business, watch_licenses, watch_business

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
